title: Why One Holiday Has Two Names
summary:
On October 12, 2026, many Americans will mark a holiday. Some call it Columbus Day. Others call it Indigenous Peoples' Day.

Columbus Day honors Christopher Columbus, an explorer from Italy. He arrived in the Americas on October 12, 1492. But Indigenous peoples, including Native Americans, had already lived there for thousands of years. Critics say his arrival led to Native Americans being treated badly.

In 1977, Native American leaders suggested a new name: Indigenous Peoples' Day. In 1992, Berkeley, California, became the first city to use it. Now more than 100 cities and several states do. In 2021, President Joe Biden officially recognized the holiday.

Not everyone wants a new name. Many Italian Americans say Columbus Day celebrates Italian culture, not Columbus himself.

History can be complicated. No matter which name people use, the holiday is a time to think about the past.
why_it_matters: Kids may hear both names at school, and learning why helps them understand history from different points of view.
